cues: Look at a beam of light end on, as if it were coming straight at you.
The electric field of the wave vibrates across the beam, at right angles to the direction of travel.
In light from a lamp or the Sun, that direction changes at random millions of times a second, as one atom after another emits its short wave train.
text: Look at a beam of light end on, as if it were coming straight at you. The electric field of the wave vibrates across the beam, at right angles to the direction of travel. In light from a lamp or the Sun, that direction changes at random millions of times a second, as one atom after another emits its short wave train. That is unpolarized light.
